original: Standardized achievement testing does not measure the full spectrum of cognitive development in learners across diverse learning contexts. Multiple-choice formats inherently fail to capture the reasoning processes students employ when solving complex problems in authentic settings. Cognitive load theory suggests that time-constrained examinations systematically disadvantage those with slower information processing speeds, regardless of actual subject competence. The persistent gap between measured performance and true ability remains a recognized limitation in educational measurement.
